Article Title: 'This is treason': Rahul Gandhi revives 'vote chori' charge after report of rift within EC
Article Text:
EC rejects reports of differences

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday revived his "vote chori" charge against the Election Commission and accused election officials of committing "treason".In a post on X, Rahul said, "I am telling the EC and election officials clearly: What you are doing is wrong. This is treason, this is against the country. Do not forget that. The time will come when we will catch you. You will not be able to escape."His remarks came after an Indian Express report claimed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections to the poll panel's actions at least 14 times over the past 10 months during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The report said the commissioners had flagged issues relating to the addition and deletion of voters as well as the handling of voter data.Senior Congress leaders KC Venugopal and P Chidambaram also stepped up their attack on the poll panel following the report.Chidambaram said the opposition had already contended that several decisions concerning the SIR were wrong and questioned how Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's view could become the decision of the Commission if the two Election Commissioners had taken a contrary position."The Supreme Court has repeatedly held that if the decision-making process is flawed or wrong, the decision will also be flawed or wrong. The opposition has contended that many decisions concerning SIR were wrong. Now, it is revealed that the decision-making process was also wrong," Chidambaram said."If two ECs have taken a contrary view, how could the CEC make his view the 'decision' of the ECI? All decisions of the ECI in recent years should be reviewed by a Parliamentary Committee. Meanwhile, the SIR process should be suspended immediately all over the country," he added.Congress general secretary KC Venugopal also targeted CEC Gyanesh Kumar and demanded his removal."There is no doubt remaining. Mr Gyanesh Kumar has no right to remain in office. How the hell can one man, acting on His Master's orders, strike off names at whim? How can he sideline fellow Constitutional officers to only take blatantly illegal steps that put our democracy in danger?" Venugopal said."The right to vote is an essential Constitutional power given to every citizen, the fundamental bedrock of our democracy. If it is to be taken away, due process must be followed with utmost probity," he added.The Election Commission, however, rejected reports of differences within the poll panel over the SIR and said all decisions related to the exercise were taken unanimously.Officials told news agency PTI that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi did raise concerns over some aspects of voter roll deletion and database handling, but these did not amount to disagreement with the final decisions taken by the Commission.EC sources said all decisions of the Commission, including those relating to the SIR, had the approval of Sandhu, Joshi and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Officials also pointed out that the law governing the Election Commission, as well as a Supreme Court judgment, provides that decisions should, as far as possible, be taken unanimously. Where unanimity is not possible, the majority view prevails.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi accuses election officials of committing "treason" Congress leaders KC Venugopal and P Chidambaram also step up attack on the poll panel. Election Commission rejects reports of differences over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR)

Article Title: Kharge backs Ladakh’s Sixth Schedule demand, seeks justice for four killed in Leh firing
Article Text:
Kharge stands with Ladakh’s Sixth Schedule demand

NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Wednesday said the party stood firmly with the people of Ladakh in their demand for meaningful constitutional safeguards, including Sixth Schedule status, to protect the Union Territory’s land, employment opportunities, fragile environment, culture and identity.In a post on X, Kharge said four young people were shot dead in Leh a year ago during protests demanding democratic and constitutional rights for the people of Ladakh."A year ago, four young people were shot in Leh during the agitation for the Democratic and Constitutional rights of the people of Ladakh. On Martyrs’ Day, we pay our solemn homage to them and stand in complete solidarity with their families," Kharge said in a post on X."The judicial inquiry into the tragic events of September 24 must establish the full truth, ensure accountability and deliver justice without fear or favour. The people of Ladakh have waited long enough for their legitimate aspirations to be addressed," he added.On September 24, 2025, police in Leh opened fire during violent protests demanding statehood and constitutional safeguards for Ladakh, killing four people.Kharge said that the Congress party "stood firmly" with their demand for meaningful Constitutional safeguards, including the Sixth Schedule, to protect Ladakh's land, employment, fragile environment, culture and identity.Meanwhile, Ladakh authorities on Tuesday promised a new framework under Article 371 to provide constitutional safeguards tailored to the Union territory’s specific needs.In an interaction with prominent community members in Leh, Chief Secretary Ashish Kundra indicated broad agreement on the need for such safeguards. “The protection should cover our land, employment, culture, environment and natural resources,” he said.Kundra said the new framework being worked out “considering the aspirations of Ladakhis does not exist anywhere else in the country”.The draft is expected to be discussed at the next meeting with Ladakh groups in the first week of October. The last meeting between the Centre and Ladakh representatives was held in Delhi on September 9.
Article Summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the party stood firmly with the people of Ladakh in their demand for meaningful constitutional safeguards, including Sixth Schedule status. Four young people were shot dead in Leh a year ago during protests demanding democratic and constitutional rights for Ladakh.

Article Title: Shouldn’t punish for refusing to sing ‘Vande Mataram’: Supreme Court
Article Text:
SC disagreed with the suggestion that the recognition of all six stanzas was not in concord with a ‘secular’ Constitution.

Courts can’t dictate what national song should be: SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Tuesday agreed to examine the legality of penal consequences if a person does not sing the national song due to religious beliefs or conscientious objection, but declined to adjudicate whether ‘Vande Mataram’ should comprise two or six stanzas, saying it was best left to Parliament’s wisdom.The court was hearing a petition by Carnatic vocalist T M Krishna objecting to recital of the complete version of the national song on the ground that its last four stanzas invoked Hindu goddesses which may offend the religious beliefs of some communities. The amended law stipulates punishment of up to three years in jail for disrupting or preventing rendition of the song.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the field was occupied by SC’s Aug 1986 Bijoe Emmanuel vs Kerala judgment that no one could be penalised for not singing the national anthem if he showed respect to it by standing in silence.Seeking the Centre’s reply in two weeks, the bench said, “nobody’s Article 25 rights or the right of a conscientious objector should be violated”.It said the Bijoe Emmanuel case ruling had never been challenged and was still the law of the land. The Centre must consider the issue raised in the PIL from that perspective, it said.The bench added that if a conscientious objector did not sing one or all stanzas of the national song, he would not be subjected to criminal prosecution.Appearing for Krishna, senior advocate S Muralidhar argued that ‘Vande Mataram’ must be confined to two stanzas, as done by Congress Working Committee in 1937 due to strong opposition by Muslims, whose faith does not permit idol worship.The hearing was marked by the bench disagreeing with the suggestion that the recognition of all six stanzas as the national song was not in concord with a “secular” Constitution and a heated exchange between solicitor general Tu-shar Mehta and Muralidhar.Muralidhar’s argument that the law-making process, where Parliament made singing of all six stanzas of Vande Mataram mandatory, was not inclusive as it did not fully accommodate public opinion had Mehta angrily retorting that law-making could not be made subservient to the “diktat of Naxalite ideas”.Justice Bagchi was sceptical of the argument that singing all six stanzas would undermine the constitutional mandate of secularism, which is a sine qua non for constitutional governance.Justice Bagchi told Muralidhar, “Nothing can be more strong or positive secularism than the US constitution. But the American national anthem uses the word ‘God’. The national song, not national anthem, paying homage to a particular form of God will not perhaps impact secularism. But your point is about whether someone who is a conscientious objector can be subjected to penal consequences. We will examine it.”Muralidhar said all six stanzas were thrust upon people after 80 years and not singing it invited penal consequences. “That is what is most worrying,” he said.The SC said, “Penal consequences we will examine. But the state is best suited to declare what the national song is and articulate national aspirations. If these kinds of issues are debated, then this would be the most unfortunate thing for the nation. Courts cannot dictate what the national song should be.”Mehta said the petition was meant to create sensationalism and persuaded the court not to issue notice while assuring that Centre would file a response.The bench said, “We may not issue notice. But the law of the land as declared by SC (in Bijoe Emanuel case) governs the acts of the state. That declaration has not been questioned. There is no dispute as to what the national song is. It is for the democratically elected state to decide what the national song is, four stanzas or two stanzas. But nobody’s Article 25 rights or the right of a conscientious objector should be violated.It is not for the court to second-guess the national sentiment or aspirations associated with ‘Vande Mataram’.”Mehta said it was not for the petitioner to decide whether the national song should be of two or six stanzas. “Those who could not stall the amendment to Prevention of Insults to National Honours Act in Parliament are now bringing the issue to the court,” he added.
Article Summary: Supreme Court agrees to examine the legality of penal consequences if a person does not sing the national song due to religious beliefs or conscientious objection. The court declined to adjudicate whether ‘Vande Mataram’ should comprise two or six stanzas, saying it was best left to Parliament.

Article Title: History refuses to leave J&K as assembly debates Hari Singh, Sheikh Abdullah anniv holidays
Article Text:
The Opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLAs staged a walkout from the Jammu and Kashmir Assembly on Tuesday in protest against the remarks by ruling National Conference (NC) MLAs over the holiday declared on the birth anniversary of Maharaja Hari Singh.

SRINAGAR: The birth anniversaries of J&K’s last Dogra ruler Maharaja Hari Singh and National Conference founder Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah were the subjects of a heated debate in the assembly Tuesday, as a demand was raised that either both days should be marked as public holidays or none.NC member Abdul Majeed Larmi demanded that Hari Singh’s birth anniversary on Sept 23 be withdrawn from the list of public holidays or else, the holiday on Sheikh Abdullah’s anniversary on Dec 5 be restored.BJP members vehemently objected to the suggestion for cancellation of the holiday on the former maharaja’s birthday. Congress supported NC’s demand for restoring the public holiday on Sheikh Abdullah’s birth anniversary, while favouring retaining the holiday for Hari Singh. PDP MLAs Waheed Para and Aga Muntazir Mehdi joined the exchange and raised the issue of restoring the July 13 holiday commemorating the killing of 22 Kashmiris outside Srinagar jail during a protest against the Dogra ruler in 1931.The speaker later said he did not have the authority to grant or withdraw govt holidays. In Jan 2020, the J&K administration had removed July 13 and Dec 5 from the list of public holidays, while Sept 23 was added to the list in 2022.
Article Summary: Opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLAs staged a walkout from the Jammu and Kashmir Assembly on Tuesday in protest against the remarks by ruling National Conference MLAs over the holiday declared on the birth anniversary of Maharaja Hari Singh.

Article Text:

GUWAHATI/NEW DELHI: Two Congress functionaries were injured and several vehicles damaged in Assam Monday after an alleged attack on their convoy in Samaguri where they were campaigning for the Oct 6 Nagaon assembly bypoll.AICC secretary Manoj Chouhan and Assam Mahila Congress president Mira Borthakur were injured in the incident in Nagaon district. He said Chouhan suffered chest and abdominal injuries, while Borthakur sustained head injuries.Around four vehicles, including those carrying LS MP Gaurav Gogoi and candidate Sibamoni Bora, were severely damaged, he said.Baghel Tuesday blamed CM Himanta Biswa Sarma for the attack. “The attack was nothing but a manifestation of Sarma’s panic. They have already conceded defeat and are desperately trying to intimidate us into retreating indoors.But he should know we are not people who can be frightened,” he said.In Delhi, Congress held a presser to denounce the “planned murderous attack”.Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh posted on X that it was a “shameful attempt by BJP, with the tacit approval of Election Commission, to avert a likely defeat” in the bypoll.The Assam chief minister denied BJP’s involvement and blamed the incident to internal Congress rivalry. “There is constant dispute and infighting between them,” he said.

Article Title: ‘Must act now’: Kashmiri leader urges UNHRC action over ‘worsening’ rights situation in PoJK, PoGB
Article Text:
Kashmiri urged the UNHRC to establish independent monitoring mechanisms for the two territories and seek accountability for alleged human rights violations.

Call for monitoring and accountability

Concerns over PoGB

United Kashmir People’s National Party (UKPNP) chairman Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri has urged the UN Human Rights Council (UNHRC) to take immediate action over what he described as a worsening human rights situation in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK) and Pakistan-occupied Gilgit-Baltistan (PoGB).Addressing the 63rd session of the UNHRC under Agenda Item 4, Kashmiri alleged that repression in PoJK had intensified since June 5, 2026. He cited reports of arrests, violence, deaths, injuries, alleged disappearances and restrictions on internet and mobile communications.Kashmiri called for an immediate, independent and impartial investigation into the reported violations. He also urged Pakistan to stop using force against peaceful protesters and release people he described as being arbitrarily detained."Peaceful dissent is not terrorism, and demanding rights is not a crime," Kashmiri said.Kashmiri urged the UNHRC to establish independent monitoring mechanisms for the two territories and seek accountability for alleged human rights violations He also called for the authorities to establish the whereabouts of missing persons and restore unrestricted internet and mobile communications across PoJK.The UKPNP chairman further called for the release of political prisoners in the Pakistan-occupied parts of Jammu and Kashmir.He said prolonged detention and alleged mistreatment should end."The Council must act now to safeguard the lives and fundamental rights of millions of Kashmiris," he said.On PoGB, Kashmiri raised concerns over political representation, land rights and control over natural resources. He called for genuine democratic dialogue to address the unresolved issues.He also said development projects in the region should be carried out transparently, with consultation and respect for local communities.Kashmiri concluded by urging the UNHRC to demand accountability and increase international scrutiny of the human rights situation in PoJK and PoGB.
Article Summary: United Kashmir People’s National Party (UKPNP) chairman Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri has urged the UN Human Rights Council (UNHRC) to take immediate action. Kashmiri alleged that repression in PoJK had intensified since June 5, 2026. He cited reports of arrests, violence, deaths, injuries, alleged disappearances.

Article Title: CM Dhami directs time-bound disposal of pending SC/ST atrocity cases in Uttarakhand
Article Text:
Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Tuesday chaired a meeting of the State-Level Vigilance and Monitoring Committee constituted for the effective implementation of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

DEHRADUN: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on tuesday chaired a meeting of the State-Level Vigilance and Monitoring Committee constituted for the effective implementation of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, and directed officials to ensure time-bound disposal of pending cases.Reviewing cases registered under the Act since 2024 where investigations are still pending, Dhami directed officials to examine the reasons for delays and take action on priority. He also called for close coordination among the police, administration and prosecution departments in long-pending and serious cases.The chief minister directed regular review of cases pending before special courts and asked officials to ensure the availability of special public prosecutors wherever required for effective prosecution.Dhami stressed that there should be no delay in disbursing prescribed relief to victims. He directed officials to separately review cases where relief payments have been delayed and said assistance to affected families should also extend, wherever required, to healthcare, education, security, rehabilitation and other eligible government schemes.The chief minister also directed officials to accord the highest priority to the safety of victims and their families in serious and sensitive cases.He said the education of children from affected families should not be disrupted and that eligible children should be linked with scholarships and other educational assistance schemes.According to the Social Welfare Department, the state has provisions for financial assistance to victims of atrocities under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, with assistance provided at different stages depending on the nature of the offence.Dhami further directed senior-level accountability in every district for monitoring cases under the Act and called for regular training of police personnel on its provisions, investigation of sensitive cases and appropriate conduct towards victims.He also instructed the Social Welfare, Police and Prosecution departments to jointly organise refresher training programmes and directed officials to work towards developing a digital monitoring system to track investigations, court proceedings, relief payments and other assistance.Districts where progress in investigation, disposal of cases or distribution of relief is unsatisfactory should be reviewed separately, Dhami said, adding that effective practices followed by better-performing districts should be shared with others.The chief minister also called for extensive awareness campaigns in rural and remote areas about the provisions of the Act, legal rights and assistance available to victims. He stressed that decisions taken during the meeting should not remain confined to official records and that responsibility and timelines should be fixed for every decision.The meeting was informed that 189 cases were registered under the Act in 2024 and 157 in 2025. In 2026, 116 cases had been registered up to September 15, of which 25 were under investigation.It was further informed that during 2024-25, financial assistance of Rs 228.71 lakh was provided to 205 victims; during 2025-26, Rs 143.16 lakh was provided to 127 victims; and during 2026-27, Rs 99.528 lakh had been provided to 104 victims as of September 18.Regular meetings have also been held at the state level under the chairmanship of the chief secretary and at the district level under the chairmanship of district magistrates.
Article Summary: Pushkar Singh Dhami on Tuesday chaired a meeting of the State-Level Vigilance and Monitoring Committee constituted for the effective implementation of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Act, 1989. The chief minister directed regular review of cases pending before special courts and asked officials to ensure availability of special public prosecutors.

Article Title: 'Naxalites can't make law': Heated exchange between lawyers during Vande Mataram SC hearing
Article Text:
SC hearing on Vande Mataram turns heated over 'Naxalites' remark

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What was the Vande Mataram case about?

NEW DELHI: A heated exchange broke out between senior advocate S Muralidhar and solicitor general Tushar Mehta in the Supreme Court on Tuesday after Mehta referred to “Naxalites” during arguments in a case concerning Vande Mataram.Muralidhar, appearing for Carnatic musician T M Krishna, immediately objected to the expression and repeatedly asked Mehta to withdraw it.“Law-making is as per the Constitution. Law-making cannot be as per the Naxalites idea,” news agency PTI quoted Mehta saying. His remarks came after Muralidhar questioned the manner in which an amendment relating to the national song had been enacted.“The solicitor must withdraw the expression he just used now. This is going live. I don't want an expression of the solicitor going live. I strongly object. Let the Solicitor repeat the expression he used,” Muralidhar said.Mehta maintained that he was responding to Muralidhar’s objection to the decision-making process and said Parliament had enacted the law in accordance with the Constitution.“I do not want anyone to question...he says he is objecting to the decision-making.It is as per the Constitution,” the solicitor general said.Muralidhar continued to press for a withdrawal of the remark.“He started it. Why is the Solicitor using this kind of an expression? This does not behove a law officer. I have never heard a law officer using this expression,” Muralidhar said.“You cannot challenge the Constitution,” Mehta responded.Justice Joymalya Bagchi said the exchange was creating “unnecessary tension and emotion”, while Chief Justice Surya Kant intervened and said the bench was examining only the legal issue of constitutional interpretation.“Decorum is expected of law officers,” Muralidhar said.The bench later sought the Centre’s response to Krishna’s petition challenging penal provisions relating to Vande Mataram. It also asked the government to keep in mind a 1986 judgment that protected children from penal action if they did not sing the national anthem.Muralidhar, however, raised the “Naxalites” remark again after the order was dictated and sought to place his protest on record.“The learned solicitor used an expression which does not behove a law officer. I have to register my strong protest,” he said.Justice Bagchi replied, “We have not taken note of the comments. We restrict ourselves to the Constitutional issue.”Mehta said he was not apologetic and repeated his position.“I can repeat what I said. He said he is objecting to the way in which the decision-making was done. Decision-making was by the Parliament. I said that is the constitutional way, and not what the Naxalites want. I am not sorry about it,” the solicitor general said.Muralidhar accused Mehta of “playing to the gallery” and again protested.“Your lordships will not encourage this from a law officer,” he said.“Save your arguments for the next date,” the CJI told him.Senior advocate Sanjay Hegde, who was present in court for another matter, then intervened, saying, “To have a mind of one's own is not to be a Naxalite.”Justice Bagchi said that even if someone was labelled a Naxalite, that person would not lose their constitutional rights.Mehta clarified that he was not labelling any individual a Naxalite but was referring to an ideology.After Muralidhar left and the court moved to the next matter, Justice Bagchi returned to the issue while addressing Mehta.“I tell you, at least from my personal experience, we have continuously fought against extra-constitutional forces, both as members of the bar and of the bench. Our survival and our justification with the Constitution is to defeat these forces,” Justice Bagchi said.He stressed the importance of constitutional courts and due process, saying even people accused of terrorism were entitled to equal constitutional rights and fair trials.“Why will people come to courts and not to kangaroo courts? There are kangaroo courts. Constitutional courts have the respect and credibility. Why? Because we feel, even alleged terrorists, must have equal rights,” Justice Bagchi said.Mehta reiterated that he was referring to people who did not believe in constitutional decision-making.“Solicitor, we have not taken note of the comments,” Justice Bagchi said.“I don't know why he took it personally,” Mehta said.The bench, comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, was hearing Krishna’s petition challenging penal protection given to Vande Mataram.During the hearing, Muralidhar argued that the amendment had been enacted without adequate public discussion or efforts to build a broader national consensus.“Ideally, these things should evolve as the building up of a public opinion,” he said, arguing against a “top down approach” to law-making.The court sought the Centre’s response to the plea and asked the government to consider the 1986 judgment concerning the national anthem while responding to the petition.
Article Summary: Solicitor general Tushar Mehta referred to 'Naxalites' during arguments in a case concerning Vande Mataram. Senior advocate S Muralidhar objected to the expression and repeatedly asked him to withdraw it. Chief Justice Surya Kant intervened and said the bench was examining the legal issue of constitutional interpretation.

Article Title: 'No point in having such a boastful CM': Tejashwi demands Samrat Choudhary's resignation over Jamui incident
Article Text:
Tejashwi demands Samrat Choudhary's resignation over Jamui incident

NEW DELHI: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav on Tuesday demanded Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary's resignation over the alleged harassment of two minor students, including a girl, in Jamui, saying the incident showed that "women and girls are not safe anywhere in Bihar".Addressing a presser in Patna, the RJD national working president said, "Bihar is being shamed" and alleged that the state had descended into "gundaraaj" under the BJP-led government.Tejashwi also invoked an earlier statement by Choudhary in which the chief minister had said he was ready to resign if anyone was harmed in Munger."Samrat Choudhary himself had earlier said, 'Go to Munger... if anything happens to anyone or someone is harmed, I am ready to resign,'" Tejashwi said, referring to the Jamui incident."Today, this video shows that women and girls are not safe anywhere in Bihar whether during the day or at night, at home or on the streets, in colleges or schools, or in hospitals," he said."The way crimes against women and girls are increasing in Bihar is extremely shameful. If Samrat Choudhary stands by his words, he should resign if he has the courage," Tejashwi said.He added, "If he cannot stand by what he said, then there is no point in having such a boastful chief minister."The RJD leader also accused members of the ruling alliance of trying to defend the incident. "You all must have seen the video, and the unfortunate part is that those in the ruling alliance are trying to justify it," he said.The remarks came after a video went viral on Monday showing a boy and a girl being harassed by a group of people on a roadside in Jamui. The video triggered widespread outrage, following which police arrested some of the accused.However, the main accused in Jamui molestation incident Nandan Yadav was injured in a police encounter, while he was being taken to the crime scene.Tejashwi alleged that the incident was another indication of what he described as the collapse of law and order in Bihar, saying the state was witnessing "gundaraaj".
Article Summary: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav demands Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary's resignation over the alleged harassment of two minor students in Jamui. The remarks came after a video went viral on Monday showing a boy and a girl being harassed by a group of people on a roadside.

NEW DELHI: Punjab Police on Tuesday denied issuing any advisory directing police officials to avoid wearing uniforms while going to or coming from duty.In a social media post on X, Punjab Police said that messages circulating online are fake and should be ignored, and advised personnel and citizens to rely only on official channels for information.“Punjab Police Headquarters or any other Punjab Police office under it has issued no advisory directing police personnel to avoid wearing uniform while going to or returning from duty,” Punjab Police said.“Such messages circulating on social media are fake and should be ignored," it added.This comes after state leader of opposition Pratap Singh Bajwa latched on to the advisory circulating online to target chief minister Bhagwant Mann, saying that the move reflected concerns over the safety of Punjabis and the morale of Punjab Police.In his post on X, Bajwa questioned Mann over who was in charge of Punjab’s law and order."Punjab Police personnel are now reportedly being advised not to travel in uniform and to wear it only after reaching their police stations. This is the disturbing consequence of having a Home Minister who appears more interested in taking jibes at the Opposition, political grandstanding and theatrics than in ensuring the safety of Punjabis and morale of Punjab Police," Bajwa said."When the police themselves are being told to hide their identity while commuting, it is time to ask CM Bhagwant Mann: who is really in charge of Punjab’s law and order?" he questioned.This comes after assistant sub-inspector Harjit Singh was killed in Amritsar during patrol duty. He was shot dead by unidentified assailants in the Hakima police station area.Amritsar Police Commissioner Harmanbir Singh Gill had claimed that the murder was orchestrated by an individual from Pakistan, operating abroad, who enticed the accused with money and promises of involvement in the narcotics trade.One accused was killed in a police encounter at a checkpoint on Thanda Road, while another escaped.
Article Summary: Punjab Police deny issuing any advisory directing police officials to avoid wearing uniforms while going to or coming from duty. In a social media post on X, Punjab Police said that messages circulating online are fake and should be ignored. This comes after assistant sub-inspector Harjit Singh was killed in Amritsar during patrol duty.

Article Title: 'Samrat Choudhary must resign over 'maha goonda raj': Opposition slams Bihar CM over Jamui molestation case
Article Text:
Jamui Police are investigating a harassment incident involving a minor girl; opp demands CM resignation

Congress, RJD leaders attack Bihar govt

NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut on Tuesday attacked Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary over the harassment of a minor girl and boy in Jamui, calling for the state government’s dismissal and alleging that “maha goonda raj” was prevailing in Bihar.“The Samrat Choudhary government must be dismissed. It is a government of goons. There is ‘maha goonda raj’ in Bihar,” Raut said while reacting to the incident.The remarks came after a video purportedly showing a minor girl being groped and her male companion being assaulted by a group of youths in Jamui went viral on social media.The incident has triggered a political controversy in Bihar, with Opposition parties questioning the state government’s law-and-order record and its handling of the case.Congress leader Udit Raj also criticised the Bihar government, saying the incident reflected the deteriorating law-and-order situation in the state.Reacting to the viral video, Raj referred to previous cases involving alleged crimes against minors and questioned the government's response to such incidents.“When a murder accused is the CM of the state, it is not difficult to imagine the condition in Bihar,” Raj said, adding that law and order had deteriorated in the state.Congress MP Manoj Kumar described the Jamui incident as “one that shames humanity” and questioned the government's claims about governance and women's safety.Referring to claims that “Ram Rajya” prevailed in Bihar, Kumar asked what kind of governance was in place when an incident such as the Jamui case occurred in the state.He also referred to an earlier statement attributed to CM Samrat Choudhary that he would resign if such an incident occurred. “The current Chief Minister of Bihar used to say that if such an incident came to light, he would resign and step down from his post. I have a direct question for you: what do you have to say about this?"RJD leader and Bihar LoP Tejashwi Yadav also targeted the state government.According to ADG (Law and Order) KS Anupam, the incident took place on September 19 when the minor girl had gone to take photographs with a male friend in Jamui. A case has been registered under various sections, and three arrests have been made.
Article Summary: A video purportedly showing a minor girl being groped and her male companion being assaulted by a group of youths in Jamui went viral on social media. The incident has triggered a political controversy in Bihar, with Opposition parties questioning the state government’s law-and-order record.

NEW DELHI: High court judge RC Chavan tendered his resignation from the committee set up by the Maharashtra government to prepare a draft for the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in the state.In his resignation letter dated September 19, Chavan alleged that suggestions from members, including those on framing the questionnaire to elicit detailed public views on issues such as late marriages, infertility, unstable marriages and dispute resolution, were not considered. He also claimed that a questionnaire finalised by the chairperson had already been circulated for uploading.Chavan also flagged the involvement of an officer from outside the state in the panel."Maharashtra officers may feel they are not competent to do this duty that an officer from another state had to be called," Chavan said in his resignation letter."It may also be that he did not know as to where to fit" the officer in the committee's functioning, he added.Chavan also alleged that meetings were being concluded without substantive discussion.Agenda items such as confirmation of minutes, website modifications and finalisation of questionnaires were disposed of quickly on the directions of the chairperson, he added.Agenda items such as confirmation of minutes, website modifications and finalisation of questionnaires were disposed of quickly on the directions of the chairperson, he claimed."To solve this problem, I am vacating my seat on the committee by resigning now, so that the government can fill in the blank promptly," the former judge said.The Maharashtra government in July set up the seven-member committee, headed by retired Supreme Court Justice Ranjana Desai, to draft a framework for implementing the common civil code in the state.
Article Summary: High court judge RC Chavan tendered his resignation from the committee set up by the Maharashtra government to prepare a draft for the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code. Chavan alleged that suggestions from members were not considered. He also claimed that a questionnaire finalised by the chairperson had already been circulated.

Article Title: 'No complaint received by SC/ST cell from Sahil Wakode': IIT-Bombay professor on student suicide case

Faculty forum stages march in support of Prof Surya

‘Doolla acted as per institute rules’
