NEW DELHI: IIT Bombay faculty forum president and professor Rajkumar Pant has rejected allegations against professor Suryanarayana Doolla following the death of second-year BTech student Sahil Wakode, saying the institute's SC/ST cell had no record of the student approaching it with a complaint in the months preceding his death.Pant said he spoke to IIT Bombay deputy director professor Ravindra Gudi, who confirmed that the SC/ST cell had issued a notice stating that there had been no attempt by Sahil to approach the cell in the previous three or four months.“There was absolutely no attempt by the late Sahil to approach the cell over the last three or four months. No complaint was recorded by him — forget about a formal complaint; he had not even approached the SC/ST cell for anything,” Pant said.Addressing allegations against Professor Doolla, Pant said faculty members were required to discharge their duties in accordance with institute procedures and defended Doolla’s actions in the matter.“We are teachers, and we are discharging our duties as mandated by the institute while following institute procedures. Professor Doolla did the same,” he said.Pant said Doolla had previously served as dean of student affairs before taking up his current position as dean of academic affairs and described him as someone known for being helpful to students.“To expect that a person of his nature — who is known to be very helpful to students — would do this is unreasonable,” Pant said.He said there could be situations where faculty members had to act firmly and that Doolla had acted according to the rules.“I'm personally convinced that he is not the kind of person who would indulge in these kinds of acts,” Pant said.His remarks come amid protests by IIT Bombay students following Sahil's death. Student representatives have said their protest was not intended to justify cheating or academic misconduct, but was aimed at raising concerns over institutional systems and seeking reforms.
Article Summary: IIT Bombay faculty forum president and professor Rajkumar Pant has rejected allegations against professor Suryanarayana Doolla. Pant said the institute's SC/ST cell had no record of the student approaching it with a complaint in the months preceding his death. Pant described Doolla as someone known for being helpful to students.

Article Title: 'Made a mistake by telling him to tolerate it': Grieving parents demand arrests in IIT Bombay student suicide case
Article Text:
IIT-Bombay student Sahil Wakode died by suicide





MUMBAI: “I made a mistake by telling him to tolerate the situation.” This was the regret expressed by the mother of IIT Bombay student Sahil Wakode, who was found dead in his hostel room last week.Sahil’s parents on Tuesday demanded the arrest of the institute’s director Shireesh B Kedare and professor Suryanarayana Doolla, news agency PTI reported.Sahil’s mother, Sonali Wakode, said she and her husband had met their son in his hostel room on September 13, when he told them he was being tortured and harassed.Speaking to ANI, she said they tried to reassure him and advised him to focus on his studies, believing he had a bright future ahead.“We tried to give him moral support and advised him to focus on his studies because he had secured admission to IIT and had a bright future ahead. In hindsight, I feel that telling him to tolerate the situation was our mistake,” she said.She added, “We persuaded him, told him that he was doing great and his future was bright. Probably, that’s where we faltered as parents. Had we taken him back home with us, our child would have been alive today.We know how the system works, but he was just a 19-year-old kid.”The parents made the remarks after visiting the Mumbai Police Crime Branch office, where they demanded a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding their son’s death and action against those found responsible, news agency PTI reported.Sonali claimed Sahil had told his parents that he was being tortured, abused and humiliated on the basis of his caste, PTI reported.“He specifically told us that professor Suryanarayana Doolla would say, ‘I am from an upper caste and you are from a lower caste.’ According to what Sahil told us, this had been continuing for around three months,” she claimed.Sahil’s father Ravindra Wakode also alleged that Doolla had told his son that he belonged to an upper caste while Sahil belonged to a lower caste.“He used to tell him that he is from the upper caste while Sahil is from the lower caste. He also told him, ‘I will implicate you in some wrong thing and will remove you.’ This had been happening for the past three months,” Ravindra said.He said that when Sahil narrated his ordeal, he advised him to tolerate the situation for the sake of his future.“When he narrated his ordeal, I advised him to bear it a bit for the sake of his future,” he said, speaking to ANI.The parents demanded the immediate arrest of Kedare and Doolla.Sahil’s mother said she had full faith in the Crime Branch and wanted the allegations recorded in the FIR to be examined thoroughly.“I have full faith in the Crime Branch and request that the investigation into my son Sahil’s death be completed fairly, thoroughly, and strictly in accordance with the FIR,” she said.“The allegations and circumstances recorded in the FIR must be properly investigated, and appropriate action should be taken against those found responsible,” she added.The mother also objected to the institute’s initial claim that Sahil had allegedly been caught using an AI platform during an examination.She said anyone making allegations of cheating must provide evidence and questioned what she described as a change in IIT Bombay’s position on the matter.“I am also concerned by what appears to be a change in IIT Bombay’s position or statements regarding these allegations. I request the authorities to examine this carefully and determine whether such allegations have any evidentiary basis or whether they are diverting attention from the issues raised in the FIR,” she said.Ravindra also defended his son’s academic record, saying Sahil had cleared the JEE Advanced examination without using unfair means or cheating.“My child was good at academics. It’s not easy to crack JEE Advanced. Look at his All India rank. He didn’t clear JEE Advanced by using unfair means or cheating,” he said.Meanwhile, a senior Crime Branch official said the statements of Sahil’s parents had been recorded, PTI reported.Statements of IIT Bombay officials, including professor Doolla, were yet to be recorded and they would be summoned for questioning soon, he said.IIT Bombay has said Prof Suryanarayana Doolla was temporarily relieved of his administrative duties pending an investigation.He continues as a professor and head of the Department of Energy Science and Engineering.The institute has also apologised for its earlier communication about the circumstances preceding Sahil’s death, saying those details remained subject to investigation.Sahil, a second-year BTech student in the Department of Energy Science and Engineering, was found hanging in his hostel room on the Powai campus on September 18 evening, hours after being caught allegedly using a mobile phone to access ChatGPT during a mid-semester examination.The allegations made by Sahil’s parents are part of the ongoing Crime Branch investigation.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: IIT Bombay student Sahil Wakode was found dead in his hostel room last week. His parents have demanded the arrest of the institute's director Shireesh B Kedare and professor Suryanarayana Doolla. Sonali Wakode claims Sahil had told his parents he was being tortured, abused and humiliated on the basis of his caste.

Article Title: Kushner, Witkoff meet Iran mediators for over 3 hours: All you need to know
Article Text:
Kushner, Witkoff hold 3-hour meeting with Iran mediators amid Trump’s threats

Who was involved in the meeting?

Trump had threatened to ‘annihilate’ Iran

What Trump said about the possible deal

What happens next?

US President Donald Trump said US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were part of the American team that met with Iranian officials and mediators in New York, with the talks lasting around three hours as Washington and Tehran face renewed pressure to reach an agreement.Trump described the meeting as a "very good meeting" but provided few details about who represented Iran or what was discussed. The talks came shortly after Trump warned in his address to the United Nations General Assembly that he could "annihilate" Iran if an agreement was not reached.Speaking during his bilateral meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Trump said, "The meeting went very well. It ended an hour ago. It was a meeting that lasted for three hours...It was a very good meeting..."Trump later said the Iranian officials involved were "not the highest level, but it's something", according to AP.Trump said Witkoff and Kushner met with mediators involved in efforts to reach a deal with Iran."Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with the mediators on the Iran deal. The mediators were here...A lot of things are working out very well," Trump said.The engagement came amid renewed diplomatic activity around the UN General Assembly in New York. Earlier on Tuesday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump was open to meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian during the gathering, although he said such engagement would depend on whether it could produce a constructive outcome.US and Iranian communications had previously taken place through mediators, including Qatar and Pakistan. The latest meeting marks another attempt to keep diplomatic channels open despite the continuing conflict between Washington and Tehran.The meeting took place just hours after Trump's address to the UN General Assembly, where he said he faced a choice between reaching a deal with Iran and taking further military action."I have a big decision to make," Trump said. "Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before, maybe one of the greatest in the Middle East or even the world. Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?"Trump also called on Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and return to negotiations. Reuters reported that his UN speech combined threats of further action with indications that a diplomatic agreement could still be possible.Trump suggested that Iran had a choice between further conflict and an agreement that could allow the country to rebuild."I can't imagine why they wouldn't want to do it... In one case, it's obliteration and the other alternative is potential greatness. It could be a great country,” he said.Trump has previously said that preventing Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons remains a central objective of US policy. Rubio also said earlier Tuesday that any potential engagement would need to address that issue.The meeting does not by itself indicate that a deal has been reached. Trump described the talks positively but did not announce an agreement or provide details of the issues discussed.Trump also met with leaders and senior officials from Gulf Cooperation Council countries and Jordan on Tuesday to discuss the Iran conflict, while the UN General Assembly provided an opportunity for multiple diplomatic contacts around the war.The latest engagement comes as the conflict continues to affect regional security and global energy markets, particularly because of the importance of the Strait of Hormuz to international oil and gas shipments.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump said US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with Iranian officials and mediators in New York. Trump described the meeting as a "very good meeting" but provided few details about who represented Iran or what was discussed. The talks came shortly after Trump warned in his address to the United Nations General Assembly that he could "annihilate" Iran.

Article Title: Kentucky man won $167.3 million Powerball jackpot in 2025; now arrested for fifth time after being found intoxicated in Walmart car park
Article Text:
Police found Kentucky Powerball winner asleep in a running Mustang

How James Farthing won Kentucky's record Powerball prize

Florida arrest came shortly after the jackpot win

February arrest involved an intimidation charge

Burglary and marijuana charges followed in March

July domestic violence case involved strangulation allegations

Fifth arrest adds to Farthing's legal cases

James Farthing, a Kentucky man who won a $167.3 million Powerball jackpot in April 2025, has been arrested for the fifth time since claiming the prize. The latest arrest took place on September 20, 2026, after deputies reportedly found him asleep inside a running Ford Mustang in a Walmart car park in Georgetown. Authorities charged him with being intoxicated in a public place following reports of alcohol-related impairment. The incident adds to a series of legal cases involving Farthing since his jackpot win. He had shared the historic prize with his mother, Linda Grizzle, after purchasing a $2 ticket from a Georgetown retailer.Earlier incidents included an April 2025 arrest in Florida, where Farthing was accused of kicking a sheriff’s deputy during an altercation. He later pleaded guilty to misdemeanor battery and obstruction or resisting arrest. In February 2026, he faced an intimidation charge, followed by burglary and marijuana-possession charges in March after being accused of entering a Lexington home and stealing $12,000. In July, he was arrested on domestic violence-related charges, including first-degree strangulation and fourth-degree assault. Farthing has pleaded not guilty to the domestic violence charges.The latest incident began shortly before 3 a.m. on Sunday, September 20, when a caller reported a white Ford Mustang stopped in the middle of an intersection in Georgetown, Kentucky. The vehicle later moved to a Walmart car park on Osborne Way, according to the arrest citation reported by WKYT.Deputies arrived and found the Mustang parked near an electric vehicle charging station with its engine running. Farthing was reportedly asleep in the passenger seat. Officers knocked on the window several times before he woke up.The arrest citation described several signs of impairment, including the smell of alcohol and marijuana, bloodshot and watery eyes, slurred speech and difficulty maintaining balance. Farthing was subsequently charged with being intoxicated in a public place and taken to the Scott County Detention Center.According to the arrest report, Farthing told deputies that a woman had driven him to the car park and left him there. Authorities reviewed surveillance footage, which reportedly showed no one exiting the Mustang after it entered the car park.Farthing purchased the winning Powerball ticket from Clark's Pump N Shop in Georgetown. The ticket matched the required numbers in the April 26, 2025 drawing, resulting in a $167.3 million jackpot.The Kentucky Lottery identified the prize as the largest Powerball jackpot ever won in the state. Farthing and his mother, Linda Grizzle, claimed the winnings together and announced that they would share the fortune.The win brought significant attention to the family, while Farthing later appeared in news reports concerning several encounters with law enforcement in Kentucky and Florida.Farthing's first reported arrest after winning the lottery took place in Florida in April 2025. Authorities accused him of battery involving a law enforcement officer and resisting arrest following an incident at a hotel.According to the Associated Press, officers said Farthing kicked a deputy in the face during an altercation and attempted to flee. He faced charges connected to the confrontation.The Independent later reported that Farthing pleaded guilty in the case and received a sentence of time served and $1,000 in fines.In February 2026, Farthing was arrested in Georgetown on a charge involving intimidation of a participant in a legal process. The case followed a report from a woman who contacted emergency services and said she feared for her safety.According to People, police investigated an incident at Farthing's home and reportedly found a woman hiding under a desk. Authorities also searched the property and allegedly discovered a handgun, ammunition, marijuana and drug paraphernalia.Farthing faced additional charges in March 2026 in connection with allegations of burglary and marijuana possession. Authorities accused him of entering a Lexington home and stealing approximately $12,000 in cash.The Guardian reported that investigators used security camera footage during the investigation. Farthing was later reportedly located at a casino.Local news reports said the burglary and marijuana charges were dismissed in May. The dismissal applied to those specific charges and did not resolve his other legal cases.In late July 2026, Farthing was charged with first-degree strangulation and fourth-degree assault following a reported domestic violence incident in Scott County.Police said a woman reported that a verbal argument became physical after a boating trip. According to the arrest report, she alleged that Farthing placed both hands around her neck and restricted her breathing. Authorities also reported visible marks on her neck.Farthing pleaded not guilty through his legal representative. A judge set his bond at $15,000 and ordered him to avoid contact with the alleged victim. He was also required to wear an electronic monitoring device with a notification feature.The September arrest is the fifth reported arrest involving Farthing since he won the Kentucky Powerball jackpot in 2025.The latest case concerns public intoxication in Scott County and follows the July domestic violence-related arrest. His legal proceedings remain separate from the lottery win, which he shared with his mother.As of September 23, 2026, the public intoxication case remained pending in Scott County District Court, with no confirmed outcome of the scheduled arraignment.The jackpot that promised a new beginning has instead been followed by a string of legal troubles. Fortune's wheel turns without warning, and wealth offers no guarantee of a steady life.
Article Summary: James Farthing won a $167.3 million Powerball jackpot in April 2025. He has been arrested for the fifth time since claiming the prize. The latest arrest took place on September 20, 2026, after deputies reportedly found him asleep inside a running Ford Mustang in a Walmart car park in Georgetown. Authorities charged him with being intoxicated in a public place following reports of alcohol- related impairment.

Article Title: Russian oligarch’s wedding gift to Trump Jr puts family dealings under scrutiny
Article Text:
Russian oligarch’s wedding gift for Trump Jr puts family dealings under scrutiny

Curtis seeks scrutiny of Jr's foreign ties

Russian oligarch helped fund wedding celebrations

More facts needed

A Russian oligarch’s role in Donald Trump Jr’s wedding celebrations has now sparked a call for a Senate investigation from the GOP. Republican senator John Curtis of Utah has asked the Judiciary Committee to examine whether US president Donald Trump’s son benefited financially from his proximity to the White House.Curtis, who is not a member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, made the request in a letter sent on Tuesday to committee chairman Chuck Grassley, a Republican from Iowa, and the panel’s top Democrat, Illinois Senator Dick Durbin. He asked the committee to subpoena Trump Jr over his business dealings, relationships with foreign individuals and entities, gifts and other benefits he has received, and any instances in which his relationship with President Donald Trump “was invoked or understood to provide value. ”Curtis also called for the same scrutiny of Hunter Biden, the son of former President Joe Biden.“The country should not have to accept one standard for the family of a Republican president and another for the family of a Democratic president,” Curtis wrote.The request puts a Republican senator at the centre of scrutiny of Trump’s family at a time when most Republican lawmakers have largely avoided weighing in on the president’s son.Curtis, who was first elected to the Senate in 2024, has previously vowed not to shy away from disagreements with Trump. He has publicly broken with the president several times, including rejecting Trump’s calls to eliminate the Senate filibuster.His latest criticism, however, goes beyond a disagreement over policy. Curtis last Friday described the reported wedding funding as “corruption” and said he would say more about the issue in the coming days.“A Russian oligarch paid for a lavish wedding after-party for Donald Trump Jr, which to me just stinks. It’s corruption. I don’t like it,” Curtis said in a video posted on social media.Earlier on Tuesday, Curtis also referred to the Republican-led scrutiny of Hunter Biden’s foreign relationships, writing that Republicans “nearly wore out the subpoena machine investigating Hunter Biden’s foreign relationships” and that they “should not unplug it now.”The controversy follows a report by ProPublica last week that Umar Kremlev, who has close ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin, helped pay for the rental of a private island and a fireworks show during celebrations for Trump Jr and socialite Bettina Anderson’s wedding in the Bahamas in May.Bettina Trump later addressed Kremlev’s involvement in an Instagram post signed by the couple. She described Kremlev, who is head of the International Boxing Association, as a “dear friend” who “very generously hosted two incredible nights of celebrations for us AFTER our wedding.”Though Trump did not attend his son’s wedding, he defended Kremlev’s involvement but said the money would be paid back.Curtis’ letter asks the Judiciary Committee to examine Trump Jr’s business dealings, his relationships with foreign individuals and entities, and gifts or other benefits he has received. It also seeks scrutiny of instances in which his relationship with the president “was invoked or understood to provide value.”Grassley has not yet committed to an investigation. Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, he said he was not yet familiar with the facts surrounding the case and would need to gather more information before deciding what action to take.“I’m going to take these requests seriously and sit down with staff and see what we can do,” Grassley said.He added that the process would take time and said, “it takes time, and if you were going to ask me when we're going to have a hearing, there’s no way I could answer that today.”Senate majority leader John Thune, Republican of South Dakota, also declined to offer a view, saying he did not “have an observation on that.”Still, some Republican lawmakers have indicated that they would support Curtis’ request.The developments come as a few Republicans have recently shown a greater willingness to criticise Trump’s policies after largely avoiding public breaks with him during much of his second term.Meanwhile, the ongoing war in Iran, high gas prices and mounting concerns about Republican prospects in November’s midterm elections have brought increased scrutiny of the president from within his own party.
Article Summary: Republican senator John Curtis of Utah has asked the Judiciary Committee to examine whether US president Donald Trump’s son benefited financially from his proximity to the White House. Curtis also called for the same scrutiny of Hunter Biden, the son of former President Joe Biden.

Article Title: 'Show your Aadhaar': How a ritual for wife's slain brother turned deadly in UP's Azamgarh
Article Text:
Police said the accused Arvind Singh (35) opened fire with his rifle after an argument with priests.

Demand for Aadhaar cards preceded firing

Accused barricades himself inside house

Forensic teams collect evidence





VARANASI: Two priests and a woman were allegedly shot dead by her husband during a dispute over a religious ritual in Shambhuganj village in Azamgarh on Tuesday evening.Police said the accused, Arvind Singh , 35, opened fire with his rifle after an argument with priests who had come to conduct rituals at his house. The deceased were identified as Mahendra Pathak, 60, Akhilesh Mishra, 50, and Singh’s wife Babita, 32. Two other priests escaped unhurt.According to the preliminary probe, Singh’s mother had invited the priests to perform rituals for the peace of the soul of Singh’s brother Sunil, who was murdered in 2019. Family members said Singh had opposed the ceremony and warned the priests against returning to the house.Police said Singh returned home while the ritual was underway and found his wife participating in the ceremony with four priests. He questioned their presence and later demanded to see their Aadhaar cards.An argument followed, with Singh allegedly abusing the priests before opening indiscriminate fire. Two priests and his wife were killed on the spot, police said.After the shooting, Singh allegedly locked himself inside the house with his three children, triggering panic in the village.A heavy police force surrounded the premises as hundreds of villagers gathered outside.Senior officers, including District Magistrate Ravindra Kumar, SSP Anil Kumar, DIG Sunil Kumar Singh and ADG Varanasi Zone Naveen Arora, reached the spot. An ATS commando team was also roped in as police launched an operation to bring the standoff to an end.Forensic teams examined the scene and collected evidence before the bodies were sent for post-mortem examination.ADG Varanasi Zone Naveen Arora confirmed the deaths. Police said no personnel were injured during the encounter. The circumstances leading to the shooting and the exact motive behind the killings are being investigated.
Article Summary: Police said the accused, Arvind Singh, 35, opened fire with his rifle after an argument with priests. The deceased were identified as Mahendra Pathak, 60, Akhilesh Mishra, 50, and Singh’s wife Babita, 32. Two other priests escaped unhurt.

Article Title: Sana two’s versions, contradictory medical reports led to acquittal of co-accused
Article Text:
Filed photo of victim Apple executive Vivek Tiwari





LUCKNOW: Contradictions in the testimony of prime witness Sana Siddiqui and inconsistencies between two medical examinations proved decisive in the acquittal of co-accused Sandeep Kumar on the charge of voluntarily causing hurt, a court observed while evaluating evidence in the Vivek Tiwari case.Sandeep Kumar, one of the two policemen accused in the 2018 shooting of Apple executive Vivek Tiwari, was acquitted on Sept 17 of the offence under IPC Section 323. Police had chargesheeted him for allegedly assaulting Sana during the incident.The incident took place on Sept 29, 2018, in which Vivek Tiwari (38) was shot after two bike-borne policemen signalled his SUV to stop when he was dropping Sana home.The court noted that Sana did not accuse Sandeep of assault in the first information report. It also relied heavily on her first medical examination, conducted within hours of the incident, which recorded no visible external injury.The allegation that Sandeep struck Sana on her arm with a stick surfaced later, first appearing in her second statement and then being reiterated in her statement under Section 164 CrPC and in her examination-in-chief. However, the court found that this later version did not align with medical evidence.A second medical examination recorded four injuries, on Sana’s nose, chin and left forearm. The court observed that these findings were difficult to reconcile with Sana’s claim that she was hit once on the arm with a stick. It also took note of the fact that no stick was recovered from Sandeep; instead, an INSAS rifle was recovered from him.Further doubt arose during Sana’s cross-examination, when she stated that Kalpana Tiwari, the deceased’s wife, came to her residence the morning after the incident and that her hand struck Sana during an altercation. The court held that the possibility that the injuries noted in the second medical examination were caused during this later scuffle could not be ruled out.Investigating officer Vikas Pandey also acknowledged that Sana had not reported any stick assault at the time of her first medical examination. Citing the absence of the allegation in the FIR, conflicting medical evidence, an alternative explanation for the injuries and non-recovery of the alleged weapon, the court held the prosecution failed to prove the charge beyond reasonable doubt.
Article Summary: Vivek Tiwari (38) was shot after two bike-borne policemen signalled his SUV to stop when he was dropping Sana home. Police had chargesheeted him for allegedly assaulting Sana during the incident. Contradictions in the testimony of prime witness Sana Siddiqui and inconsistencies between two medical examinations proved decisive in the acquittal of co-accused Sandeep Kumar.

Article Title: 19-year-old run over by crane outside university in Gota
Article Text:
The victim, Prerna Ninami, had left home around 11am to attend college.





AHMEDABAD: A 19-year-old BSc Biotechnology student was run over by a pick-and-carry hydraulic crane outside a private university in Gota on Tuesday afternoon. The crane operator, who fled after the accident, has been arrested.The victim, Prerna Ninami, had left home around 11am to attend college.Around noon, she was walking along the road outside the university where she studies, when a crane approaching from SG Highway hit her from behind.The crane’s left front wheel ran over her, crushing her. Paramedics of 108 EMRI services declared her dead on the spot. Her mother, Kanta Ninami, lodged a police complaint.A witness told police that the crane, bearing registration number GJ-01-RQ-2685, was being driven in a negligent manner before it struck the student.A Division police inspector A B Mori said the accused, Arunkumar Nishad, 26, is a licensed crane driver who has been operating cranes in Gujarat for six years.A case has been registered against the driver under provisions of BNS, including causing death by negligence, act endangering life or personal safety, and rash driving.
Article Summary: Prerna Ninami, 19, was run over by a pick-and-carry hydraulic crane outside a private university in Gota on Tuesday afternoon. The crane operator, who fled after the accident, has been arrested. A case has been registered against the driver under provisions of BNS.

Article Title: Deep depression triggers heavy rain in Andhra Pradesh; schools shut in 6 districts, disaster teams deployed
Article Text:
Coastal Andhra Pradesh braces for incoming moderate to heavy rains as a deep depression approaches, forcing the government to close schools for safety





VISAKHAPATNAM: Moderate to heavy rain lashed parts of coastal Andhra Pradesh on Wednesday due to the deep depression, forcing the government to close schools in Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Anakapalle districts. The government also cancelled employees’ leave and deployed teams in vulnerable areas to prepare for a possible calamity.Authorities declared a holiday for Anganwadi centres in these districts on Wednesday.The weather agency said the deep depression over the westcentral and adjoining northwest Bay of Bengal moved westwards at a speed of 7 kmph during the past six hours and lay centred about 100 km east-southeast of Kalingapatnam in Andhra Pradesh , 150 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha, 220 km south-southwest of Puri in Odisha and 180 km east-northeast of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh.It is very likely to move west-northwestwards and cross the North Andhra Pradesh-South Odisha coasts between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur, close to Kalingapatnam, as a deep depression by Wednesday night.Parts of coastal Andhra Pradesh, including Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalle, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Parvathipuram Manyam, Konaseema, Kakinada, West Godavari, East Godavari and Eluru, are likely to receive heavy rainfall on Wednesday.The weather agency said squalls with winds gusting up to 75 kmph are likely along and off the North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts from the morning of September 23 to the evening of September 24. Squally winds with speeds of 45-55 kmph, gusting to 65 kmph, are likely to prevail along and off the South Andhra Pradesh coast from September 23 to 24.The government has deployed State Disaster Response Force teams to tackle the rain and flood situation in parts of north coastal Andhra Pradesh.
Article Summary: Government closes schools in Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Anakapalle districts. Government also cancelled employees’ leave and deployed teams in vulnerable areas to prepare for a possible calamity.

Article Title: Rapper UNB attacked with rod while returning from concert in Arunachal Pradesh
Article Text:
Police attributed the delay in reporting the incident to poor mobile connectivity in the area.

(With agency inputs)





ITANAGAR: Sikkim-based rapper Ugen Namgyal Bhutia, popularly known as UNB, was allegedly attacked by a group of men in Arunachal Pradesh’s Lower Dibang Valley district, police said on Wednesday.The incident occurred around 6pm on Monday near Tiwari Gaon when UNB and his team were returning to Roing after attending a festival in Anini, police said.Two vehicles allegedly followed their car for nearly an hour before intercepting it on an isolated stretch.Eight to 10 men allegedly vandalised UNB’s vehicle with a rod and attacked him and his manager, police said.UNB suffered injuries to his head and face, besides swelling around one eye, police said.The attackers fled after spotting a truck approaching the area, they added.The incident was reported to Roing police station around 7.50pm.Police attributed the delay in reporting the incident to poor mobile connectivity in the area.Following the complaint, police alerted check gates and asked personnel to look out for vehicles matching the description provided by the victims.UNB’s manager alleged that the attackers had covered their vehicles’ number plates with mud and intercepted their car after confirming that the rapper was travelling in it.Roing police station officer-in-charge Taniya Uli said police accompanied UNB and his team to the site on Tuesday as part of the investigation.The isolated location, absence of eyewitnesses and poor network connectivity were posing challenges to the investigation, the officer said.A case has been registered under provisions relating to wrongful restraint, voluntarily causing hurt and criminal intimidation, he said.Police said they were working to ascertain the motive behind the attack and establish the identity of the accused.
Article Summary: Sikkim-based rapper Ugen Namgyal Bhutia, popularly known as UNB, was allegedly attacked by a group of men in Arunachal Pradesh’s Lower Dibang Valley district. The incident occurred around 6pm on Monday near Tiwari Gaon when UNB and his team were returning to Roing.

Article Title: 'Blackmailed with morphed pics': Gwalior teen raped by 17-year-old neighbour on day of Jamui horror
Article Text:
The boy had allegedly been stalking the Class 10 student for nearly a year, according to her family's complaint.

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you believe is the most effective way to combat online harassment? Stricter laws Strong privacy awareness Timely police action 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





BHOPAL: On the day a Class 10 student was molested on a road in Bihar's Jamui, a 16-year-old girl nearly 1,000km away in MP's Gwalior was allegedly raped by her 17-year-old neighbour after he blackmailed her with "morphed" private photos, police said.The Gwalior girl was on her way to coaching class on Saturday when her bike-borne tormentor allegedly intercepted her, telling her he would make the photos and "chats" public.He is then accused of forcing her to accompany him to a flat and raping her before dropping her near her coaching centre. The accused has been arrested.The boy had allegedly been stalking the Class 10 student for nearly a year, according to her family's complaint.The girl told the police he had repeatedly followed her around her coaching centre and later began threatening her with the photos and chat screenshots.According to the complaint, the harassment stopped briefly but the accused allegedly resumed it later, leading to Saturday's harassment and subsequent assault.
Article Summary: The Gwalior girl was on her way to coaching class on Saturday when her bike- borne tormentor allegedly intercepted her. He is then accused of forcing her to accompany him to a flat and raping her before dropping her near her coaching centre. The accused has been arrested.

Article Title: Pocso case: Granite baron Veeramani’s aide arrested
Article Text:
Granite baron R Veeramani who was arrested in relation to a Pocso





CHENNAI: The Central Crime Branch (CCB) has arrested a long-time aide of granite baron and head of Gem Granites, Veeramani, who was arrested on Aug 29 on charges of raping a minor girl.The arrested accused, Ganesan, shall be the fourth suspect in the Pocso Act case involving the sexual abuse of minor girls. Police found that Ganesan had video clippings on his mobile phone purportedly showing Veeramani in an obscene act with a minor girl but failed to inform police about it.Ganesan had worked with Veeramani’s Gem Granites for 23 years and is currently employed with Balaji Global enterprises, police said. Earlier, the Anti-Vice Squad (AVS) had registered a case against Veeramani and two of his accomplices, in connection with the rape of minor girls. The three were arrested on Aug 29 and remanded in Puzhal Central prison.During further investigation, police identified Ganesan, who had been closely associated with Veeramani for several years. Investigators are now probing the source of the video and the circumstances under which he retained it without alerting the authorities. Police are also examining his mobile phone to ascertain if he had deleted any data.The investigation has also widened into suspected financial transactions made in an attempt to influence the earlier investigation. Police are examining bank transactions and the possible use of intermediaries in the movement of funds.Veeramani, was arrested on Aug 29 after a USB drive containing a video clip that purportedly showed a juvenile girl being sexually assaulted by him in Oct 2025. Police said they identified the survivor and established that she was a minor when the alleged offence took place in 2019.
Article Summary: Ganesan had worked with Veeramani’s Gem Granites for 23 years and is currently employed with Balaji Global enterprises, police said. Police found that Ganesan. had video clippings on his mobile phone purportedly showing Veer.amani in an obscene act with a minor girl but failed to inform police about it.

Article Title: 'Bring your sisters, our boys are ready': BJP MLAs’ controversial take on Muslims in garba sparks row
Article Text:
Huzur MLA Rameshwar Sharma

BJP MLAs’ garba remarks trigger political row





BHOPAL: Controversial remarks by two BJP MLAs over the participation of Muslims in Navratri garba events have triggered a political row in MP, with Congress accusing the governing party members of "hate-mongering".Speaking at a public event in Bhopal, Huzur MLA Rameshwar Sharma questioned why Muslim youths who wanted to attend garba did not bring young women from their community to such functions.They should bring along their sisters and daughters, he said, adding that "our boys are ready". If garba was turned into a "tamasha" or used for " love jihad ", "our youth" would be ready to respond, he warned.As his remarks, reported Monday, drew criticism, Sharma doubled down, saying Muslim youths who wanted to participate in garba should "bring their sisters and daughters; our daughters and sisters also go there".Anyone attending garba should do so with a spirit of worship and devotion, he asserted, adding that those who had developed an interest in Hinduism should accept Sanatan traditions.He also reiterated his warning against what he described as attempts to use garba for "love jihad".Mhow MLA and former minister Usha Thakur, too, objected to the entry of non-Hindus into garba pandals and said those who did not worship Hindu deities should not be allowed at such functions.She claimed that 4.5 lakh Hindu girls leave with people of other faiths every year and that around nine lakh children are born the following year, but did not provide any official data or source for the figures.The BJP MLA supported campaigns by VHP and Bajrang Dal seeking restrictions on entry of non-Hindus, alleging that some people concealed their identities by applying tilak and wearing kalava before entering such venues and misled young women.Flaying the remarks, Congress state secretary Kunal Chowdhary said, "Every day, BJP leaders say things that spread hatred and spoil the image of MP."
Article Summary: Controversial remarks by two BJP MLAs over the participation of Muslims in Navratri garba events have triggered a political row in MP. Congress accuses the governing party members of "hate-mongering" Huzur MLA Rameshwar Sharma questioned why Muslim youths who wanted to attend garba did not bring young women.

Article Title: 3 preterm infants die after blaze at RIMS in Adilabad
Article Text:
There were 27 newborns and their attendants when the fire broke out in the Special Newborn Care Unit

Inquiry ordered





HYDERABAD: Three infants, including a two-day and a five-day-old baby, died after a fire broke out due to a suspected short circuit in the air-conditioning unit at the Special Newborn Care Unit (SNCU) of Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS) in Adilabad late Monday night. Two other infants who sustained injuries are also in a critical condition, hospital authorities said.While one of them is on ventilator, another is on oxygen support.Officials said that the remaining 22 newborns, who were safely evacuated from the SNCU, have either been shifted to nearby private hospitals, or are being treated at RIMS. Their condition is stable.“All the rescued newborns are being closely monitored. Those requiring oxygen support are being provided the same, and we are keeping a close watch on their condition,” said Dr P Sadhana, district medical & health officer (DM&HO), Adilabad.It is suspected that the three “extreme preterm infants”, all of them girls, died due to asphyxiation.According to preliminary probe, the fire broke out around 11.40 pm while the 27 newborns and their attendants were present inside the unit. Though the exact cause is yet to be established, it is suspected that an electrical short circuit in a window AC triggered the fire.While one of the newborns died within an hour of the incident, two others died later on Tuesday while undergoing treatment at the Government General Hospital (GGH) in Nizamabad and RIMS, respectively, in the early hours of Tuesday.“The fire resulted in the entire ward quickly filling up with smoke as the plastic from the AC burnt. We managed to contain the fire by 3am,” said D Jayatram, station fire officer (SFO), Adilabad.Based on the initial probe, the Adilabad police booked a case of unnatural or suspicious death under Section 194 of the BNSS and started an investigation.Dr Sadhana said that while 23 children were in the SNCU, four others were in a nearby ward. “As they were preterm babies, they were already in a weak condition and a few of them lost consciousness immediately due to smoke or toxic-fume inhalation,” she added.According to her, two of the deceased infants were born at 28 weeks and weighed around 1.3kg each, while the third, who was 15 days old was born at 25 weeks and weighed around 1kg. Their families belonged to surrounding mandals of Utnoor, Ichoda and Indravelli in Nizamabad.Health officials said there was a problem with the AC, which was repaired about a week ago. “Fire and electrical safety audits had also been conducted at the hospital. Around Rs 5 crore had been spent on works at the hospital, while Rs 1 crore was sanctioned for AC-related works. A meeting was scheduled later this month to discuss replacing the existing ACs with new ones,” an official said.Meanwhile, expressing grief over the incident, Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy ordered an inquiry and directed officials to submit a report on the cause of the fire.Health minister Damodar Rajanarasimha, who visited the affected newborn ward at RIMS, announced that a committee comprising experts would be constituted to conduct a comprehensive inquiry into the fire incident . He added that three safety audits - electrical, fire and civil structural - would be conducted at RIMS.The minister also assured that strict action would be taken against anyone found responsible for negligence or lapses during the inquiry.“The committee would examine the causes of the accident, safety lapses and maintenance failures, and recommend measures to prevent such incidents in the future. Comprehensive proposals would be submitted to the government based on the expert committee’s reports regarding electrical, fire and civil structural safety audits. These proposals will cover necessary repairs, additional infrastructure, renovation works, new building construction and the recruitment of additional staff at RIMS. All aspects concerning potential lapses in maintenance, monitoring and the implementation of safety standards at RIMS would be thoroughly examined,” the minister added.
Article Summary: Three infants, including a two-day and a five-day-old baby, died after a fire broke out due to a suspected short circuit in the air-conditioning unit. Two other infants who sustained injuries are also in a critical condition, hospital authorities said. The remaining 22 newborns, who were safely evacuated from the SNCU, have either been shifted to nearby private hospitals or are being treated at RIMS.

Article Title: Sant Kabir Nagar wrestler beaten to death; panchayat poll rivalry angle being probed
Article Text:
The attackers allegedly threw chilli powder into his eyes before assaulting him with sticks, rods and sharp-edged weapons.





LUCKNOW: A 35-year-old wrestler was beaten to death by a group of assailants in Bhagtan Gosainpur village of Khalilabad in Sant Kabir Nagar on Tuesday evening.The attackers allegedly threw chilli powder into his eyes before assaulting him with sticks, rods and sharp-edged weapons.A possible rivalry linked to the upcoming panchayat polls is also being examined as a motive behind the killing.The victim, Brahmanand (35), was a resident of Bhagtan Gosainpur and was known as a wrestler and district-level Kesari. The incident took place around 5.30 pm, about 10 km from the district headquarters.According to his family, Brahmanand was returning on his motorcycle after going to purchase chokar (cattle feed) when he was intercepted by 8 to 10 men around 100 metres from his house.The attackers allegedly first threw chilli powder into his eyes, causing him to lose control of the motorcycle and fall on the road. They then allegedly attacked him with sticks and sharp-edged weapons, leaving him critically injured.On being informed, family members rushed to the spot and took Brahmanand to the Community Health Centre in Khalilabad. Given his critical condition, doctors referred him to the district hospital.However, he died on the way.Following his death, family members and villagers placed the body on the Khalilabad bypass and blocked the road, demanding action against those responsible.Police officials assured them of action against the accused, following which the protesters agreed to remove the body from the road.Police took custody of the body and sent it for post-mortem examination.SP, Sant Kabir Nagar, Sandeep Meena, told TOI that an FIR against Abhimanyu, Chabiram, Rakesh Yadav, Ajay has been registered under the charges of murder on the complaint of the victim’s brother Ramakant Yadav.“We have detained some people and are questioning them,” said Meena. Investigators are probing the circumstances leading to the attack, including the reported rivalry over village headship while efforts are underway to identify and apprehend those involved.
Article Summary: A 35-year-old wrestler was beaten to death by a group of assailants. The attackers allegedly threw chilli powder into his eyes before assaulting him with sticks, rods and sharp-edged weapons. A possible rivalry linked to the upcoming panchayat polls is also being examined as a motive.

Article Title: Father breaks into smoke-filled NCU in RIMS, finds 5-day-old daughter dead
Article Text:
Though the anxious father managed to break through a glass door and enter the SNCU, it was too late.





HYDERABAD: Saleem Khan had just stepped out of RIMS' special neonatal care unit (SNCU) on Monday night when, startled by a deafening sound and thick smoke, he rushed back with his brother. Khan's five-day-old baby girl was admitted there after being born underweight at a private hospital.Though the anxious father managed to break through a glass door and enter the SNCU, it was too late. His infant had already died, allegedly due to asphyxiation."What should I tell my wife when she asks me about the baby?" an inconsolable Khan said hours after the tragedy. His wife had not yet seen their newborn daughter. A resident of Subhash Nagar in Ichoda, Khan had brought his daughter to RIMS soon after her birth, on the advice of doctors at the private hospital where the delivery took place. The child was underweight and needed care in a specialised SNCU such as the one at RIMS.On the day of the fire, Khan visited her as usual. He had barely stepped out and removed the visitor gown when an AC inside the SNCU reportedly exploded. "Doctors, nurses and security guards broke the glass doors and started bringing the babies out.Everyone was trying to rescue the infants," Khan said.The situation soon turned chaotic. About 15 minutes later, hospital officials and police reached the spot and stopped people from entering as smoke continued to fill the area. Khan said he could not find his daughter and had no way of knowing whether she had been evacuated. "My brother and I went around to the rear of the building, broke open a door and entered the ward in search of the baby. Though we found her and brought her out, we couldn't save her," the visibly distraught father said. "The baby was supposed to be our third child, after two sons.," Khan said.
Article Summary: Saleem Khan had just stepped out of RIMS' special neonatal care unit (SNCU) when he was startled by a deafening sound and thick smoke. Khan's five-day-old baby girl was admitted there after being born underweight at a private hospital.

Article Title: MP man dies in RPF custody at CSMT, Maharashtra CID to probe
Article Text:
A 34-year-old fruit vendor from MP’s Khandwa died on Sunday after he was de­tained by Railway Protect­i­on Force (RPF) at CSMT





MUMBAI: The state CID will probe into the death of a 34-year-old passenger at CSMT on Sunday, while he had been detained by Railway Protection Force (RPF).Railway officials alleged that Imran Patel, a fruit vendor from Khandwa in Madhya Pradesh who had come to Mumbai to visit Haji Ali dargah, “got aggressive” and manhandled an RPF sub-inspector, after which he was restrained. He subsequently fell unconscious in a lavatory and was pronounced dead.Patel’s family last spoke to him on the phone while he was in Mumbai. They have demanded a thorough investigation into the incident.According to a Central Railway official, Patel approached the CSMT RPF main post on Sunday at 10.18am, seeking information about trains to Khandwa. “He was behaving erratically, claiming that some people were trying to kill him. Later, he got aggressive. He hit RPF sub-inspector Aniket as well as himself. He was restrained by RPF personnel to prevent injury. Government Railway Police (GRP) was informed and five GRP personnel reached the RPF post,” the official said.Around 12.30pm, Patel sought to use the lavatory and was escorted by railway police. When he did not come out for seven to eight minutes, railway police forced the door open and found him lying unconscious.At 12.54pm, Patel was moved to St George’s Hospital where he was pronounced dead.After CCTV footage was scrutinised, images of Patel moving around CSMT station early that morning were found. He had made visits to the GRP chowky as well as the help desk. “No identity card or phone was found on him. There were two general compartment tickets — Khandwa to Bhusaval dated Sept 18, and Nashik to Dadar journey dated Sept 19,” the CR official said.Patel’s family said they got a phone call from Khandwa GRP and were connected to the CSMT GRP through them. “On learning that my brother had passed away, we rushed to Mumbai. For most of the day on Monday, a post-mortem examination was carried out at J J Hospital and videographed. When we were finally shown his body, there were marks on his nose and face. We left the city on Monday night with his body to carry out the last rites at Khandwa,” said Patel’s brother, Irfaan.“We do not know what happened at CSMT after my brother approached the RPF. We suspect he was assaulted. If he was complaining about some people trying to kill him, why wasn’t he made to feel safe by the security agencies? We want justice. If a thorough inquiry is not carried out, we will file a petition in a court in MP,” added Irfaan.GRP have recorded an accidental death case. Prashant Waghunde, superintendent of police, state CID, confirmed on Tuesday that they were to initiate an investigation.Patel is survived by his wife and three children.
Article Summary: Imran Patel, a fruit vendor from MP’s Khandwa, died on Sunday after he was de­tained by Railway Protect­i­on Force (RPF) at CSMT. He had come to Mumbai to visit Haji Ali dargah. Railway officials alleged that Patel “got aggressive’ and manhandled an RPF sub-inspector.

Article Title: Goa police decline casino director’s demand for escort, pilot vehicles
Article Text:
Goa police have declined Shrinivas Nayak's request for a police escort due to ongoing threats following an armed attack





PANAJI: Goa police have declined Majestic Pride Group director Shrinivas Nayak’s request to provide him with a police escort and pilot vehicles — a privilege currently afforded only to chief minister — as the Porvorim shootout case has been worked out.TOI was the first to report about Nayak’s request to Goa police to provide him security.“Goa police do proper threat assessment. Based on these grounds, security is provided. When the application was made, and the points raised, Nayak must not have been aware of the progress of the case. We have worked out the case in such circumstances. There is no need to provide him security as requested,” inspector general of police (IGP) K R Chaurasia told TOI.Chaurasia said that Nayak will get the same security that is being provided to the common man. Goa police have arrested seven persons in connection with the Porvorim shootout.Nayak demanded protection, citing continuing threats to his life after an alleged armed attack and attempt to murder on Aug 28.In Goa, apart from chief minister, not even other cabinet ministers get police escort and pilot vehicles.In his letter to police, Nayak said that two unknown armed assailants carried out a targeted attack upon him at Hotel Neo Majestic by opening fire at him.“The circumstances surrounding the incident, including the movements and conduct of the assailants prior to the attack, give rise to a serious apprehension that the attack was premeditated and planned. A complaint in respect of the said incident has already been lodged with the Porvorim police station and the matter is presently under investigation,” he said.“During the said armed attack, my personal bodyguard was compelled to discharge rounds from his licensed firearm solely for the purpose of protecting my life and repelling the continuing armed attack. Pursuant to the investigation, the firearm of his bodyguard has been attached by the police for the purpose of forensic and ballistic examination. Consequently, the armed protection which was otherwise available to me through my bodyguard has, for the present, been materially affected,” he said.More importantly, the two assailants who carried out the attack, as well as the persons, if any, who may have planned, instructed, financed, facilitated or otherwise been involved in the attack, are yet to be identified and/or apprehended and continue to remain at large, he said.
Article Summary: Goa police have declined Majestic Pride Group director Shrinivas Nayak’s request to provide him with a police escort and pilot vehicles. Nayak demanded protection, citing continuing threats to his life after an alleged armed attack and attempt to murder on Aug 28. In Goa, apart from chief minister, not even other cabinet ministers get police escort.

Article Title: Newlyweds found dead in UP a day after temple wedding
Article Text:
Police said the exact cause of death would be determined after forensic findings and autopsy reports are received.





LUCKNOW: A newly married couple was found dead inside their room in Siddharthnagar district on Tuesday morning.The groom, Deshraj Chauhan, 24, was found hanging, while his bride, Anita Chauhan, 22, was discovered lying on the floor in her bridal attire. The couple had exchanged vows a day earlier at the Tekdhar Baba temple in Bansi.After the wedding on Monday afternoon, family hosted a reception at Deshraj’s home in Janiyajot village. Relatives and neighbours attended the gathering, which continued until about 11 pm. The newlyweds also participated in the celebrations, family members said.The deaths came to light around 9 am on Tuesday when Anita’s maternal aunt, Meenakshi, went to wake her after she did not come out of the room. When repeated calls received no response, she pushed open the door and found the couple inside. Anita was lying on the floor and Deshraj was hanging, police said.Meenakshi’s cries alerted other family members, who rushed in and brought Deshraj’s body down before informing the police.Police said the exact cause of death would be determined after forensic findings and autopsy reports are received.Deshraj, who worked at a pani puri stall in Delhi, had returned home about two weeks ago. Anita was from Karjahwa village, around 15 km away. Their marriage had been fixed three months earlier and was initially scheduled for May 2027, but the families decided to advance it after the couple stayed in touch and Anita visited his home.Circle Officer Shivendu Singh said police were examining all angles.
Article Summary: The groom, Deshraj Chauhan, 24, was found hanging, while his bride, Anita, 22, was discovered lying on the floor in her bridal attire. The couple had exchanged vows a day earlier at the Tekdhar Baba temple in Bansi.

Article Title: IIT-Bombay student’s parents 'driven out' of Mumbai in 'private car'
Article Text:
Sahil Wakode's parents claim they were forcibly removed from Mumbai by unidentified individuals despite their wishes





MUMBAI: In a dramatic turn early Wednesday morning, the parents of IIT-Bombay student Sahil Wakode alleged that they had been driven out of Mumbai in a “private car” despite repeatedly telling the driver that they intended to remain in the city and begin a hunger strike outside the Powai institute. By early morning, the family said they had reached the Karanja Lad area of Washim district.The family, accompanied by their advocate Nikhil Wakode, had earlier spoken to the media outside the Crime Branch office in Bandra and later outside the IIT-Bombay campus in Powai.According to Wakode, at some point in Powai after leaving IITB gate, they were asked by men who were not in uniform to shift to another vehicle. “We were asked to change the car by some people who were not in uniform. I was wondering why my clients were being taken in a private car when they had their own vehicle. So I too sat along with them. I don't know the name of the officers, they were in mufti,” Wakode said.Sahil’s father, Ravindra Wakode, said the family repeatedly asked the driver where they were being taken. “He kept saying, ‘I am dropping you home’,” Wakode said, who added, they were also tired and sleepy.The family claimed they made it clear that they did not want to return home and instead planned to begin a hunger strike outside the IIT-Bombay campus from Wednesday morning.“I have taken permission for that,” Wakode said.Wakode claimed that police vehicles initially followed the private car, but were no longer visible after the vehicle entered the Samruddhi Expressway. “We then told the driver that we wanted to use the washroom and got off the vehicle,” he said.Wakode said the family was now returning to Mumbai and that he remained determined to begin the hunger strike outside IIT-Bombay.“I want justice for my son. Do you realise that 100 hours have passed and no action has been taken against the offenders?” he said.
Article Summary: Sahil Wakode's parents claim they were forcibly removed from Mumbai by unidentified individuals despite their wishes. By early morning, the family said they had reached the Karanja Lad area of Washim district. The family claimed they made it clear that they did not want to return home.

Article Title: Chennai metro phase-2 inauguration awaits PM Modi’s confirmation
Article Text:
Chennai Metro's Phase-2 initially ready for passenger use since February, covering 14.64km, still awaits an inauguration date from Prime Minister Modi despite securing safety clearance





CHENNAI: Nearly seven months after receiving safety clearance, the first stretch of Chennai Metro’s Phase-2 network is still waiting for an inauguration date from Prime Minister Narendra Modi , leaving a 14.64km line closed to passengers.Sources said CMRL was awaiting confirmation from the Prime Minister’s Office. “Initially, we were told the inauguration could happen at the end of Sept, but till Sept 21, there was no update. We think it may happen in the first week of Oct,” the source said.The inauguration could be clubbed with other programmes during the Prime Minister’s visit to Chennai, officials said. However, there was no confirmation of the PM’s visit to the city as of Tuesday.The 14.64km Poonamallee Bypass-Vadapalani stretch, comprising 11 elevated stations, received conditional provisional approval from the Commissioner of Railway Safety (CRS) to commence commercial operations in Feb. The stretch is the first section of Phase-2 to be ready for passenger operations. It is part of Corridor 4, which will eventually run 26.1km between Lighthouse and Poonamallee Bypass. Phase-2 comprises three corridors totalling 118.9km.After the initial approval, CMRL complied with the conditions and subsequently received clearance, with relaxations in train speed and frequency, in May. The inauguration was earlier delayed amid the state assembly elections, as CMRL had planned a grand event with the Prime Minister opening the line. In Aug, officials had also said the Prime Minister might inaugurate the Chennai stretch along with an Indore Metro corridor through video conferencing from New Delhi.That plan did not materialise. Indore’s 11km Priority Corridor-2 was inaugurated on Sept 5 by Union housing and urban affairs minister Manohar Lal in the presence of Madhya Pradesh chief minister Mohan Yadav. With the new corridor, Indore’s operational Metro network expanded to about 17km.For commuters, the prolonged wait means a line that has cleared the safety process remains unused. “Many of us are waiting for the line to open. We want to switch from our bikes to Metro trains for our daily commute. A seven-month delay when the stretch is ready is beyond reasonable,” said S Prashanth, an Iyyappanthangal resident who works in Vadapalani. “Why is the PM so busy giving a date for inauguration, and why is the Tamil Nadu govt waiting for the PM? Why can’t they inaugurate it with ministry-level officials?” he said.
Article Summary: The 14.64km Poonamallee Bypass-Vadapalani stretch, comprising 11 elevated stations, received conditional provisional approval from the Commissioner of Railway Safety (CRS) to commence commercial operations in Feb. The stretch is the first section of Phase-2 to be ready for passenger operations. It is part of Corridor 4, which will eventually run 26.1km.

Article Title: Peacemaker with a warning to annihilate: The major contradictions in Trump's UN speech
Article Text:
Donald Trump used much of his address at the UN to list his achievements. (AP photo)

Peacemaker to annihilator

US President Donald Trump returned to the United Nations podium Tuesday wearing two very different hats. One moment he was the global peacemaker who had "ended eight wars", the next he was threatening to wipe out Iran.The gap between these two versions captures the uncertain order Trump has built, or perhaps enabled, during his second term in the White House.Trump used much of his address to the General Debate of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly to list his achievements, much as he did a year ago when he cast himself as the standout contender for the Nobel Peace Prize. This year, though, the prize went unmentioned. Instead, his tone hardened, with attacks on the International Criminal Court (ICC), the UN's climate agenda and Unesco.Trump also pointed to his effort to launch a "Board of Peace" in January, which appeared another swipe at the UN, with him at one point suggesting his new creation might end up replacing it.Ironically, within a month of the board's creation, the US and Israel launched a joint military operation against Iran, one that has continued in some form since."Since I took office, it has been my great honour to settle eight wars, and in so doing, become friendly with the leaders of many of those countries.It was a great honour to do it. Numerous of these wars have gone on for many years and even decades," he told the assembled leaders.He credited his success to what he called "very special relationships", along with the use and threat of tariffs.Among the conflicts he claimed to have resolved were the disputes between Cambodia and Thailand, Kosovo and Serbia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, Pakistan and India, and Armenia and Azerbaijan, as well as the war in Gaza.He repeated a claim India has long rejected, that he brokered peace between India and Pakistan last year."The Prime Minister of Pakistan, terrific man, said that Donald Trump was responsible for saving 30 million lives and probably many more than that," Trump said.India has always maintained the ceasefire came from direct talks between the two countries' military operations chiefs, with Pakistani DGMO seeking the truce amid Operation Sindoor.He also mentioned Russia and Ukraine, saying his team is "working very closely" with both sides. "We will get that one done. It's going to happen, I think, more quickly than people understand," he said.Having spent much of the speech basking in the image of a dealmaker, Trump turned to Iran, warning that Tehran must either negotiate with Washington or face destruction.Iran would never be allowed to have nuclear weapons, he said, adding that he faces "a big decision to make.""Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before, maybe one of the greatest in the Middle East or even the world? Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic, and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?"He went further still, asking, "Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?" He then predicted a deal was more likely once the midterm elections were over, since Iran was "waiting to see how I do in the midterm election," despite Trump not being on the ballot himself.Lo and behold, Trump's speech offered a portrait of a President who saw no contradiction in claiming the mantle of peacemaker while reserving the language of annihilation for those who resist his terms.
Article Summary: Trump used much of his address to the General Debate of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly to list his achievements. This year, though, the prize went unmentioned. Instead, his tone hardened, with attacks on the International Criminal Court (ICC) and Unesco.

Article Title: Divorced woman can seek maintenance even if divorce was on ground of desertion: Allahabad HC
Article Text:
Allahabad HC





LUCKNOW: The Allahabad High Court’s Lucknow Bench has held that a divorced woman can demand maintenance from her former husband even if the divorce was granted to the husband on the ground of desertion, if she has not remarried and is unable to maintain herself.Justice Ram Manohar Narayan Mishra made the observation while allowing a criminal revision petition filed by Suneeta against an order of the Family Court, Sultanpur, which had rejected her maintenance claim.The woman had filed a maintenance case under Section 125 CrPC in 2009, alleging that her husband and in-laws had harassed her over additional dowry and demanded Rs 1 lakh, a motorcycle and a colour television. The husband denied the allegations and claimed that she had deserted him and was unwilling to live with him.During the proceedings, the husband obtained an ex-parte divorce decree on September 25, 2014, on the ground of desertion. The bench also noted material indicating that he had subsequently remarried and that the name of the second woman had been recorded as his wife in his service records.Delivering the verdict, the bench held that a divorced woman continues to be treated as a wife for the limited purpose of claiming maintenance under Section 125 CrPC.The mere fact that the divorce was granted on the ground of desertion does not, by itself, bar her claim.The court observed that a divorced woman is entitled to maintenance until she remarries or becomes capable of maintaining herself through her own earnings, subject to the applicable legal conditions.It held that the Family Court had erred in rejecting the woman's claim in toto. While the court said her entitlement for the period before the divorce would have to be examined separately, it directed that her claim from September 25, 2014, the date of divorce, be considered afresh.The court also held that her minor son was entitled to maintenance until attaining majority, after accounting for any amount already received through Army authorities.The matter was remanded to the Family Court for fresh consideration. Meanwhile, pending fresh adjudication by the family Court , the bench has directed the husband to pay Rs 4,000 per month as interim maintenance to the woman.
Article Summary: Allahabad High Court’s Lucknow Bench has held that a divorced woman can demand maintenance from her former husband even if the divorce was granted to the husband on the ground of desertion. Justice Ram Manohar Narayan Mishra made the observation while allowing a criminal revision petition filed by Suneeta against an order of the Family Court, Sultanpur, which had rejected her maintenance claim.

Article Title: Bihar cop shoots sister dead with service pistol, later kills self
Article Text:
SP (West) Sanket Kumar said family bickering over the sister’s mental health may have led to the incident.

(With inputs from agency)





PATNA: A Bihar police constable allegedly shot his sister dead with his service pistol before shooting himself in Patna’s Danapur area, officials said on Wednesday.City superintendent of police (West) Sanket Kumar said the incident might have been the fallout of frequent bickering within the family over the sister's mental health challenges."Danapur police station received information on Tuesday evening that two persons sustained bullet injuries. Upon reaching the spot, police found that the constable had fatally shot his sister and then killed himself inside his house," the officer told news agency PTI.Police recovered the service revolver from the spot.The bodies were sent for post-mortem examination, the SP said.
