City superintendent of police (West) Sanket Kumar said the incident might have been the fallout of frequent bickering within the family over the sister's mental health.

Article Title: Donald Trump wants to rename AI; says: 'artificial' makes AI sound fake, renames it 'super intelligence'; It is exactly the opposite of...
Article Text:
Trump picked 'super intelligence' after two social media polls

US president says whoever wins super intelligence wins the world

Superintelligence already has a very different meaning in AI research

US President Donald Trump wants the world to stop saying "artificial intelligence". Speaking at the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Tuesday (September 22), Trump said the US will now officially call the technology "super intelligence", or SI. His reason is simple: the word "artificial" makes it sound fake. "It makes it sound fake, and it is not fake. It's actually amazing," he said.The change, according to Trump, will cover all US government documents. "From this point forward, all of the United States documents, and hopefully the world's, will be changed to use the much more accurate term, super as opposed to artificial," he told the assembly. There is no word yet on when the switch will happen or how it will be carried out. Trump himself did not sound too sure. "Let's see if I have any power. Maybe I do, and maybe I don't, we're gonna find out pretty soon," he said.The idea did not come out of nowhere. On Saturday (September 19), Trump posted on X and Truth Social that "many people think that the words 'Artificial Intelligence' are inaccurate, and very ineloquent." He then asked followers to vote on three options: Superior Intelligence, Extreme Intelligence and Supreme Intelligence."Superior Intelligence" took an early lead with around 39% of the vote and later crossed 41%. Then, on Monday, Trump ran a second poll that pitted "Superior Intelligence" against a new entry, "Super Intelligence". The new option won comfortably, and Trump started using "SI" in his posts almost immediately. So the name he announced at the UN was not even on the original ballot.The same weekend, Trump said he was forming an "AI Force", modelled on the Space Force from his first term. He also promised to name an AI czar soon, adding, "Only High I.Q. individuals need apply!" He did not explain what either would do.At the UN, the rename came wrapped in a larger message about the AI race. "Whoever wins super intelligence wins," Trump said, adding that the US is "leading now over China by a lot."He was clear that his government will not slow the technology down. "I'm not going to stifle growth of something that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution," he said. He added that the Department of Justice and other law enforcement bodies would "watch it closely" and step in if needed. In the same breath, he argued that the fear around AI gets it wrong. "In fact, it is exactly the opposite of what it purports," he said.Trump also lumped AI safety warnings with climate change and the "Russia, Russia, Russia hoax". Earlier in the week, he had called the backlash against AI a hoax pushed by his political rivals. The comments come after an Anthropic researcher resigned, saying leading AI companies believe the technology "could kill us all by the end of the decade." Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has since proposed a plan to "pace the frontier", which OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk appeared to back.There is a catch with Trump's pick. In AI circles, "superintelligence" is not a new word. Philosopher Nick Bostrom described it back in 1997 as "an intellect that is much smarter than the best human brains in practically every field." Researchers use it for hypothetical future systems that outperform humans across most tasks. Today's chatbots are not there yet, and Bostrom's work is largely about the risks such systems could pose."Artificial intelligence" itself has no legal status that a president can overwrite. Computer scientist John McCarthy coined it in a 1955 proposal for a Dartmouth College conference, co-authored with Claude Shannon, Marvin Minsky and Nathaniel Rochester. At the time, rival labels such as "automata studies" and "complex information processing" were also doing the rounds. "AI" won, and it has stuck for 70 years. It is even part of company names like OpenAI.Trump has renamed things before. The Gulf of Mexico and Denali got new labels, and digital maps in the US updated within days. A word used by millions of engineers, companies and users every day is a different test. Government files may say SI soon. Whether anyone outside Washington follows is the part Trump admitted he cannot predict.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump wants the world to stop saying "artificial intelligence" Trump said the US will now officially call the technology "super intelligence" or SI. The change, according to Trump, will cover all US government documents. There is no word yet on when the switch will happen or how it will be carried out.

Article Title: Hazaribag man drowns while fishing in lake
Article Text:
Hazaribag:





A man drowned in a lake of Hazaribag city while fishing, police said on Monday. The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Officer in-charge of the Lohsighna police station Rohit Kerketta said, “Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake but did not return till late in the night. They began a search and found his fishing gear and a tiffin box on the bank of the lake. His body was later found floating in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.”
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.

Article Title: Saurav Das alleges Delhi Police trying to build a ‘cooked-up anti-national story’ against CJP members
Article Text:
(CJP) chief spokesperson Saurav Das (File Photo)





NEW DELHI: CJP spokesperson Saurav Das on Tuesday accused the Delhi Police of allegedly trying to build an “anti-national” narrative around people associated with the protests, claiming that artificial intelligence, deepfakes and doctored chats were being used as part of the purported investigation.In a post on X, Das said he had been “reliably informed” by people in the establishment that the Delhi Police was continuing to investigate the group and attempting to link it to an “anti-national” narrative."We have been reliably informed by friends in the establishment that the Delhi Police is still busy trying to investigate us and somehow fit us into a cooked-up “anti-national” story. We are told this impossible feat of creative writing now requires deepfakes, AI, doctored chats and god knows what else, all of course at the taxpayer’s expense. Quite an expensive writers room I must say.""A gentle reminder to Delhi Police: the protesters have been granted permanent immunity in matters relating to the protests. And even otherwise, writing fiction is not part of the Police Manual. You are not going to get the Booker Prize or Nobel Prize for Literature. So please stop wasting everyone’s time and public money. Instead, go investigate the PG Mafia, Hospital Mafia, and Education Mafia in Delhi," the CJP spokesperson said in the post."The Delhi Police may also wish to refresh its memory about what happened when certain BRUTAL directions issued by Amit Shah to the Home Secretary and the then Police Commissioner were flat out refused by the two to be implemented, as a consequence of which its Commissioner was removed barely three-four days before the Parliament March," he added further."In any case, why go through all this jugaad? If Delhi Police has any questions about us, the protests, the Supreme Court judgment, please call all three of us, me, Dipke, Ashutosh anytime. We will happily come together to the new Police Commissioner’s office and subject ourselves to unlimited questioning. No deepfakes will be required then. Originals will come," Das said.He also alleged that the purported use of deepfakes, AI and edited chats was being funded with taxpayers’ money. He also called on the Delhi Police to investigate what he described as the “PG Mafia, Hospital Mafia, and Education Mafia” in the capital instead.Das further referred to alleged directions issued by Union home minister Amit Shah to the Home Secretary and the then Delhi Police commissioner, claiming that the two officials had refused to implement them and that the commissioner was subsequently removed days before the Parliament March.He did not provide details of the alleged investigation or the sources on which his claims were based in the post.Das also offered to appear before the Delhi Police along with CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and co-convener Ashutosh Ranka if the force had questions about the protests or the Supreme Court judgment."If Delhi Police has any questions about us, the protests, the Supreme Court judgment, please call all three of us, me, Dipke, Ashutosh anytime. We will happily come together to the new Police Commissioner’s office and subject ourselves to unlimited questioning. No deepfakes will be required then. Originals will come," he wrote in the post.
Article Summary: CJP spokesperson Saurav Das accused the Delhi Police of allegedly trying to build an “anti-national” narrative around people associated with the protests. He claimed that artificial intelligence, deepfakes and doctored chats were being used as part of the purported investigation.
